lines.japanese: 昨日に引き続き、今日もまた、か…
lines.english: Again today, just like yesterday…

lines.japanese:
やっと眠れるようになって、
めでたく昼夜逆転してる俺の生活リズムが、
ますます狂っていく…
lines.english: Now that I could finally sleep, my days and nights had obligingly reversed themselves. This was only going to make the wreck of my schedule worse.

lines.japanese:
「あ～はいっ！
はいはいはいはい…ちょっと待ってろって！」
lines.english: “Coming! Yes, yes, yes—just wait a second!”

lines.japanese:
跳ね起きついでに時計に目をやると、８時。
空のこの色から察するに、午後。
lines.english: I sprang upright and glanced at the clock. Eight. Judging by the color of the sky, eight in the evening.

lines.japanese:
起きてると思われても仕方ない時間だな。
どうやら非常識な訪問を怒る訳にもいかないらしい。
lines.english: It was a perfectly reasonable hour to assume I was awake. Apparently I had no grounds for complaining about an inconsiderate visit.

lines.japanese:
ま、俺の家に直接押しかける奴なんて、
勧誘や詐欺でもなければ数えるほどもいない。
lines.english: Besides, I could count on one hand the people who would come directly to my apartment, unless they were selling something or running a scam.

lines.japanese: 「武也かぁ？」
lines.english: “Takeya?”

lines.japanese: 「よっ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「よぉっ！」
lines.english: “Heeey!”

lines.japanese: こいつは…『数えるほど』に含めてなかった。
lines.english: She had not been included in my count.

lines.japanese:
だって、レポートも終わり、
ゼミも終わり、打ち上げも終わり、
そして今年も終わり…
lines.english: Her paper was done, our seminar was over, the party was finished, and the year itself was almost gone.

lines.japanese:
そんな完璧休日モードの日々に、
平日ですらサボリ魔のこいつが、
まさか大学の近くをうろついてるなんて…
lines.english: These were days of perfect vacation idleness. The idea that this habitual truant—who barely came near the university on weekdays—would be roaming the neighborhood now had never occurred to me.

lines.japanese:
「わ、無精髭～！
ね～、すりすりさせて～♪」
lines.english: “Ooh, stubble! Let me rub my cheek against it!”

lines.japanese:
「ま、ま、待て！
和泉！　お前何しに来やがった！？」
lines.english: “W-wait! Izumi! What the hell are you doing here?”

lines.japanese:
…まぁ、いきなり抱きついて頬をくっつけてくる方は、
ある程度は危惧してたけど。
lines.english: Though I had, to some extent, feared the possibility of her throwing herself at me and pressing her cheek to mine.

lines.japanese:
「何しにきやがったは酷いなぁ。
せっかく女の子が一大決心して来たってのに」
lines.english: “That’s a horrible welcome. A girl works up all her courage to come here, and this is what she gets?”

lines.japanese: 「…そのココロは？」
lines.english: “And what, exactly, did you work up your courage to do?”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、ローテーションの一角。
そろそろ泊めてくれる友達のネタが尽きてきて」
lines.english: “Mm, you’re one stop in the rotation. I’m starting to run out of friends who’ll let me stay over.”

lines.japanese: 「また家に帰ってないのかよ」
lines.english: “You still haven’t gone home?”

lines.japanese:
どうやら、和泉家の母子断絶は、
未だにそこそこ深刻なレベルで推移しているらしい。
lines.english: Apparently the estrangement between Chiaki and her mother was still fairly serious.

lines.japanese:
…このネタを使われると、
人のことが言えなくなってしまうので勘弁して欲しい。
lines.english: I wished she wouldn’t play that card. It made me painfully unqualified to criticize her.

lines.japanese:
「昨日まで泊まってた部屋のコが帰省しちゃってさ。
さすがに暖房の入らない冬休みの研究室も辛くってね～」
lines.english: “The girl I was staying with until yesterday went home for the holidays. And even I can’t face winter break in an unheated seminar room.”

lines.japanese: 「他を当たってくれ他を」
lines.english: “Try someone else.”

lines.japanese:
「他って言ってもさぁ…
あとは同じゼミの知り合いくらいしかいないけど」
lines.english: “Who else is there? I only have a few acquaintances from our seminar left.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそっちに」
lines.english: “Then try them.”

lines.japanese: 「みんな春希と同じ性別だけど？」
lines.english: “They’re all guys, like you.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、仕方ないか。ちょっと電話貸してね。
携帯の電池ヤバいことになっちゃっててさぁ。
だからここにも連絡できなかったんだよね～」
lines.english: “Oh well, I suppose I have no choice. Let me borrow your phone a minute. My cell’s almost dead. That’s why I couldn’t call before coming.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いやお前、それは…」
lines.english: “N-no, wait, that’s…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、その…」
lines.english: “Well, um…”
“Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「…充電器買えよ」
lines.english: “Buy a charger.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、待て！
お前、ゼミの男友達なんて顔知ってる程度だろ！」
lines.english: “W-wait! You barely know any of the men in our seminar!”

lines.japanese:
「でも多分泊めてくれるよ？
なんなら賭けてみる？」
lines.english: “They’d probably let me stay anyway. Want to bet?”

lines.japanese: 「…そんな危ないことすんな」
lines.english: “Don’t do anything that dangerous.”

lines.japanese:
「んふふ～、
お邪魔しま～す」
lines.english: “Hee-hee. Then don’t mind if I do.”

lines.japanese: こいつ、ネゴシエーションの才能だけは俺より遙かに上だ。
lines.english: Her talent for negotiation, at least, far surpassed mine.

lines.japanese: 熱い水流が頭と体の両方を覚ましていく。
lines.english: The hot water woke both my mind and my body.

lines.japanese:
石鹸とスポンジで痛くなるくらい全身をこすり、
ついでに皮膚の感覚も取り戻していく。
lines.english: I scrubbed myself all over with soap and a sponge until it hurt, restoring some feeling to my skin in the process.

lines.japanese:
女を部屋に招き入れ、すぐにシャワーを浴びるという、
ある意味『それっぽい』行動を取ってるのは、
別にそれっぽいことをするつもりとかではなく…
lines.english: Letting a woman into my apartment and then jumping straight into the shower certainly looked suggestive. Not that I planned to do what it looked like…

lines.japanese:
和泉に指摘された無精髭の処理と、
その根本原因の解決。
つまり、しばらく風呂に入っていなかったからだ。
lines.english: I needed to deal with the stubble Izumi had pointed out—and with its underlying cause. Namely, that I hadn’t bathed in some time.

lines.japanese:
いくら相手が和泉とは言え、あまりにエチケット違反。
…にしてもあいつ、よくこんな臭くて汚い俺に
平気で抱きついてきやがったな。
lines.english: Even if it was only Izumi, this was a gross breach of basic etiquette. Though how she’d managed to hug me without flinching when I was this filthy and foul-smelling was beyond me.

lines.japanese:
別に、あいつの口車に乗った訳でも、
誘惑に屈した訳でもないんだからな。
lines.english: I hadn’t fallen for her patter. And I certainly hadn’t yielded to temptation.

lines.japanese:
ただ、和泉の場合、嘘のはずの脅し文句を
『ま、いっかぁ』程度の割り切りで
実行したりしそうだからしょうがないんだ。
lines.english: The problem was that Izumi might take a threat she never meant to carry out, shrug, and carry it out anyway.

lines.japanese:
あの日以来、二日連続、二度目の
強制的なコミュニケーション。
lines.english: For the second day running since that night, someone had forced me back into contact with the world.

lines.japanese:
しかも今度は声だけじゃなく、
直接相手と接してる。
lines.english: This time it wasn’t only a voice over the phone. Another person was physically here.

lines.japanese:
望まないまま、許されないまま…
それでも俺の生活は、徐々に元へと戻っていく。
lines.english: Without wanting it, without being forgiven… and still my life was gradually returning to what it had been.

lines.japanese: 「むぐ、んぐ…」
lines.english: “Mmf, mm…”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、たまにはピザもいいね。
まぁあたしとしては春希の手料理の方が理想だけどさ」
lines.english: “Mm, pizza’s nice once in a while. Though ideally, I’d rather have something you cooked.”

lines.japanese:
「ちゃんとサラダも食え。
栄養のバランスを考えて食事しろ」
lines.english: “Eat your salad too. Try to have something resembling a balanced diet.”

lines.japanese:
「思ったよりも食べるね春希。
ずっと寝てた割には」
lines.english: “You eat more than I expected, Haruki. For someone who’s been sleeping all this time.”

lines.japanese:
「…エネルギーの消費以上に
補給してなかったからな」
lines.english: “I hadn’t eaten enough to replace even the little energy I’d used.”

lines.japanese:
ほぼ四日ぶりの、しかも胃に負担のかかる重い食事は、
何故だかひたすら喉を通った。
lines.english: It was my first real meal in almost four days, rich enough to punish an empty stomach, yet it went down with inexplicable ease.

lines.japanese:
正直、美味いかまずいかなんて判断できるほど、
舌の感覚が戻ってきてる訳じゃない。
lines.english: My sense of taste hadn’t recovered enough to tell whether it was good or bad.

lines.japanese:
それでも、途中で音を上げるかと思っていた俺の胃は、
なかなか図太くチーズとパイの塊を受け入れた。
lines.english: But my stomach, which I had expected to protest halfway through, proved remarkably hardy as it accepted one mass of cheese and crust after another.

lines.japanese: 「このっ、このぉっ！」
lines.english: “Take that! And that!”

lines.japanese:
「そんなにタバスコかけるな。
しかも俺の領域にまで侵食してきやがって」
lines.english: “Stop pouring on so much Tabasco. You’re even invading my half now.”

lines.japanese:
昨日から、やっと眠れるようになった。
そして今日、風呂に入った。髭を剃った。
lines.english: Yesterday, I had finally begun to sleep. Today, I had bathed and shaved.

lines.japanese:
こうして、やっと食えるようになった。
というか、食う気になった。
lines.english: And now I could finally eat again—or at least wanted to.

lines.japanese: 「んぐ、ん…んんっ！？」
lines.english: “Mmf… mm—mmph!?”

lines.japanese:
「だから一気に詰め込むなと…
お茶飲むか？」
lines.english: “That’s why you shouldn’t cram it all in at once. Want some tea?”

lines.japanese: 「ビ…ビール」
lines.english: “B-beer.”

lines.japanese: 「…はいはい」
lines.english: “Fine, fine.”

lines.japanese:
俺がこんなに普通に食えてるのは、多分、
目の前でこうして美味しそうに飯を食う奴がいたから…
lines.english: I was probably eating so normally because someone across from me was devouring her food with such obvious pleasure.

lines.japanese:
「ん、んぐ、んぐ、んぐ………ぷはぁっ！
うあぁぁぁ～、染みるぅ」
lines.english: “Mm, glug, glug, glug… Ahhh! Oh, that hits the spot.”

lines.japanese:
「流し込むだけのために一缶空ける奴があるか。
お前、途中から目的変わってたろ？」
lines.english: “Who drains a whole can just to wash down one bite? Somewhere along the way, drinking the beer became the point, didn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 不本意ながら、認めざるを得ない。
lines.english: Much as I disliked it, I had to admit the truth.

lines.japanese:
「あ、最後の一つのピザ、
春希に譲ってあげるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, you can have the last slice, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか？　じゃあ遠慮なく」
lines.english: “Really? Don’t mind if I do.”

lines.japanese:
「その代わり、
これで半分以上はあんたが食べた計算になるんだから、
ワリカン率は７：３…せめて６：４に！」
lines.english: “In return, since that means you ate more than half, we split the bill seventy-thirty—or at least sixty-forty!”

lines.japanese: 「…なんてせせこましい計算してんだ和泉は」
lines.english: “What kind of miserly arithmetic is that, Izumi?”

lines.japanese:
「い、いや～、
さすがに外泊を繰り返してたせいで先立つものが…」
lines.english: “Well, you see… all this staying away from home has taken a toll on my finances.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、ピザ代くらいは俺が全額負担する」
lines.english: “Forget it. I’ll pay for the pizza.”

lines.japanese:
「え、マジ？
いくつ食べたとか関係なく全部春希のおごり！？」
lines.english: “Seriously? You’re buying the whole thing no matter how much either of us ate?”

lines.japanese: 「…既にビール代も全額負担してるしな」
lines.english: “I’m already paying for all the beer.”

lines.japanese:
「わ～い、春希太っ腹～、愛してる～！
じゃあ最後の一つも遠慮なく…」
lines.english: “Yay! Haruki, you’re the best! I love you! In that case, I’ll just help myself to the last—”

lines.japanese:
「それはスポンサーに譲れ。
資金提供の絶対条件だ」
lines.english: “The sponsor gets that slice. It’s a nonnegotiable condition of funding.”

lines.japanese: 「…なんてせせこましい権利を振りかざすかな春希は」
lines.english: “What a petty little funding condition to hold over me.”

lines.japanese:
麻理さんに引き続き、和泉までもが、
俺を、もとの世界へと導いてくれている。
lines.english: First Mari, now Izumi: they were leading me back into the world I had left.

lines.japanese:
「そいえばさ～、
冬休み入ってからどっか遊びに行った？」
lines.english: “By the way, have you gone anywhere fun since winter break started?”

lines.japanese: 「ずっと引きこもり」
lines.english: “I’ve been holed up here.”

lines.japanese:
食事をするのも久しぶりなら、
家事をするのも当然久しぶりだった。
lines.english: It had been as long since I’d done housework as it had since I’d eaten.

lines.japanese:
カチカチに乾燥してたナイロンタワシ。
最初、こびりついて出なかった台所用洗剤。
ちょっと赤錆の混じってた水。
lines.english: The nylon scrubber had dried stiff. The dish soap was crusted shut. The first water from the tap came out flecked with rust.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　彼女と遊びに行ったりは？」
lines.english: “Really? You haven’t gone anywhere with your girlfriend?”

lines.japanese:
「…そもそも俺に彼女がいるって話は
一体どこから来てるんだ？」
lines.english: “Where did this story about me having a girlfriend even come from?”

lines.japanese:
俺が何もしなかった数日間の傷痕は、
部屋の中の色々なところで見つかった。
lines.english: The scars left by my days of doing nothing could be found all over the apartment.

lines.japanese: 「え？　前に言ってなかったっけ？」
lines.english: “What? Didn’t you say you had one before?”

lines.japanese:
「言ってないだろそんなこと。
妙なカマかけるな」
lines.english: “Of course I didn’t. Stop fishing.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあなに？　春希ってば、
冬休みにどっこも遊びに行く予定ないの？」
lines.english: “Then what? You don’t have a single plan to go out and enjoy winter break?”

lines.japanese: 「バイトがあるんだよバイトが。俺は忙しいの」
lines.english: “I have work. I’m a busy man.”

lines.japanese:
「ずっと引きこもってたって言わなかったっけ？
しかも、つい１０秒ほど前」
lines.english: “Didn’t you just say you’d been holed up here? Roughly ten seconds ago?”

lines.japanese: 例えば…
lines.english: For example…

lines.japanese:
こんな初歩的なツッコミすら論破できないくらい、
コミュニケーション能力が低下してたりとか。
lines.english: For example, my social skills had deteriorated so badly that I couldn’t even muster a comeback to a jab that obvious.

lines.japanese: 「何か言ったか？」
lines.english: “Did you say something?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？」
lines.english: “Who knows?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、こっち…」
lines.english: “Then this one…”

lines.japanese: 「…違うな、こっちだ」
lines.english: “No, not that one. This one.”

lines.japanese: 「あ…っ」
lines.english: “Ah—”

lines.japanese:
「はい上がり～♪
これであたしの何連勝だっけ？」
lines.english: “And I’m out! How many wins in a row is that?”

lines.japanese:
「くっそ～！
一度はババに手をかけてたのに～！」
lines.english: “Damn it! You touched the joker once—I nearly had you!”

lines.japanese:
手元に残った唯一のカードであるジョーカーを放り投げ、
今日の自分の運のなさを嘆く。
lines.english: I hurled away the joker, the only card left in my hand, and cursed the day’s miserable luck.

lines.japanese:
食後のババ抜きの戦績は１０連敗を含む２勝１６敗。
客観的に見ても一方的と言える差がついている。
lines.english: Our after-dinner Old Maid record now stood at two wins and sixteen losses for me, including a ten-game losing streak. By any objective measure, it was a massacre.

lines.japanese:
「だって春希、反応が露骨なんだもん。
そっちにババが行った時点で勝負あったも同然」
lines.english: “Your reactions are too obvious. The second the joker reaches your hand, the game is practically over.”

lines.japanese:
「なんでそんなに強いんだよ…
実はカードに印とか付けてないだろな？」
lines.english: “How are you this good? You haven’t marked the cards, have you?”

lines.japanese:
確かに勝ったときは、
一度も自分の手元にジョーカーが来ないまま、
最後まで逃げ切ったケースだけだった。
lines.english: Indeed, my only victories had been the games in which the joker never reached my hand at all.

lines.japanese:
「よくさぁ、『嘘をつくと耳を触る』とか、
そういう癖で見抜くとか言うじゃん」
lines.english: “People always talk about tells, right? Like touching your ear when you lie.”

lines.japanese: 「…俺にもそういうのがあるのか？」
lines.english: “Do I have something like that?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、そんな単純なモノじゃないって。
人間の反応って奴はさぁ」
lines.english: “No. Human reactions aren’t that simple.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなのか？」
lines.english: “They aren’t?”

lines.japanese:
「仕草や息遣いや口数や顔色やその他諸々…
相手の色んな反応を全部見て総合的に判断しないと」
lines.english: “You have to take in everything—their gestures, breathing, how much they talk, the color in their face—and judge it all together.”

lines.japanese: 「そこまで観察してんのかよ…」
lines.english: “You watch people that closely?”

lines.japanese:
「それだけじゃないよ。
こっちは逆にそういうの全部コントロールして、
相手に逆の意図を誤解させるように仕向けるの」
lines.english: “That’s only half of it. You also control all those things in yourself, so the other person reads the opposite of what you mean.”

lines.japanese:
「お前…
心理学専攻した方が良かったんじゃないか？」
lines.english: “You should have majored in psychology.”

lines.japanese:
あまりにも大げさに聞こえるその人間操作術が、
これだけの連敗を重ねた今となっては、
真実味をもって頭に届く。
lines.english: Her methods of manipulating people had sounded absurdly grandiose. After this many losses, though, they were beginning to seem disturbingly plausible.

lines.japanese:
最初に和泉が提案してきたポーカーを、
『ギャンブル性の高いゲームは禁止』って
断っておいて本当に良かった…
lines.english: Thank God I had turned down her first suggestion, poker, on the grounds that it involved too much gambling.

lines.japanese:
「ん～、理論には興味ないんだよね。
あくまでも実践というか、現場主義というか」
lines.english: “I’m not interested in the theory. I’m more of a hands-on, learn-in-the-field kind of person.”

lines.japanese: 「将来、詐欺師にでもなるつもりかよ」
lines.english: “Planning to become a con artist?”

lines.japanese: 「今でも…似たようなものかもね」
lines.english: “Maybe I already am… something close to one.”
“Izumi…?”

lines.japanese:
と、観察眼とポーカーフェイスと
人間操作術に長けた同級生は、
ほんの少し自嘲気味に笑った。
lines.english: My classmate, gifted at reading people, keeping a poker face, and manipulating them, smiled with the faintest trace of self-mockery.

lines.japanese:
「と、それはともかくさ～、
もうちょっと歯応えのある勝負がしたいよあたしは。
何か他に遊ぶものないの？」
lines.english: “Anyway, forget that. I want a game with a little more bite. Don’t you have anything else we can play?”

lines.japanese: 「トランプ以外だと…ＵＮ○とか？」
lines.english: “Other than playing cards… UN○?”

lines.japanese:
「相変わらず娯楽の少ない部屋だよねぇ。
あたしの友達でゲーム機持ってないのって
春希くらいだよ」
lines.english: “This apartment is as starved for entertainment as ever. You’re the only friend I have who doesn’t own a game console.”

lines.japanese:
「文句があるならもう寝ろ。
そして夢の中で一進一退の好勝負でも
繰り広げててくれ」
lines.english: “If you’re going to complain, go to sleep. You can have a thrilling, evenly matched contest in your dreams.”

lines.japanese:
「仕方ないなぁ…
じゃあ目標を２０連勝に上方修正して
ババ抜き続けますか～」
lines.english: “Oh, well. Let’s revise my target upward to twenty straight wins and keep playing Old Maid.”

lines.japanese: 「…お前はどれだけ俺を苦しめれば気が済むんだ？」
lines.english: “How much suffering will it take to satisfy you?”

lines.japanese:
引いてきたのはダイヤの５…
手持ちのスペードの５と合わせて場に捨てる。
lines.english: I drew the five of diamonds, paired it with the five of spades in my hand, and discarded them.

lines.japanese:
和泉は、やはり俺のカードの山から
何度も札を持ち替えると、
しっかりハートの８を引いて場に捨てた。
lines.english: As usual, Izumi moved her hand back and forth over my cards several times, then confidently drew the eight of hearts and laid down its pair.
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese:
続いて、ひときわ気合いを入れて
引いてきたカードはクラブのＪ。
手持ちのダイヤのＪと合わせて場に…
lines.english: Then, with exceptional determination, I drew the jack of clubs and moved to pair it with my jack of diamonds…

lines.japanese:
…なんて、俺の手の内にババがある以上、
向こうから引いてきたカードが無害なのは自明の理。
lines.english: Of course, since the joker was in my hand, it was self-evident that every card I drew from her was harmless.

lines.japanese:
今さら言っても仕方のないことだけど、
二人きりのババ抜きって…結構不毛だよなぁ。
lines.english: Too late to complain now, but Old Maid between two people was a remarkably futile game.

lines.japanese:
次に和泉が引いていったのはクラブのＫ。
…こいつ、本当にババ引かねぇ。
lines.english: Next, Izumi drew the king of clubs. She seriously never picked the joker.

lines.japanese: 俺が引いたのがダイヤの２。
lines.english: I drew the two of diamonds.

lines.japanese: 和泉が引いたのがハートの９。
lines.english: Izumi drew the nine of hearts.

lines.japanese: あと、３枚…
lines.english: Three cards left…

lines.japanese: 「…ねぇ、春希」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 俺が引いたのがスペードの３。
lines.english: I drew the three of spades.

lines.japanese:
結局、いつも通り、和泉の二択に持ち込まれた。
残る切り札は、俺のポーカーフェイスのみ…
lines.english: Once again, it had come down to Izumi choosing between my final two cards. My poker face was the only trump card I had left.
“Want to?”

lines.japanese: 「……しない」

そのギリギリの駆け引きは、
お互い、カードから目を離さないまま行われた。
lines.english: We conducted that knife-edge negotiation without either of us taking our eyes from the cards.

lines.japanese:
…カードの方は、二枚ともテーブルの上に、
数字を見せたままこぼれ落ちてしまっていたけれど。
lines.english: Though both cards had already slipped faceup onto the table.

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why not?”

lines.japanese: 「お前こそ、なんでそんなこと言うんだ？」
lines.english: “Why would you even suggest it?”

lines.japanese:
二人とも、完全に主語を省略してたけど、
いくら俺でも、この状況でその意味がわからないほど
鈍くはいられないようだった。
lines.english: Neither of us had said what “it” was. Even I wasn’t obtuse enough to misunderstand under the circumstances.

lines.japanese:
「ん～、だって春希落ち込んでるみたいだから、
元気づけてあげようかな～って」
lines.english: “You looked depressed. I thought I might cheer you up.”

lines.japanese:
………和泉の脚が、
テーブルの下で、俺に触れてくる。
lines.english: Under the table, Izumi’s leg touched mine.

lines.japanese:
「お前は…
落ち込んでる暗い男がいたら、いつも、その…
そうやって、慰めたりしてるのか？」
lines.english: “Do you… always comfort gloomy men that way when they’re feeling down?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、こんなこと言うの初めてだよ。
春希だけだよ」
lines.english: “No. I’ve never said this to anyone before. Only you.”

lines.japanese: 「…何だって？」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 「ん～、でもどっちが本当の目的なんだろ」
lines.english: “Mm… I wonder which one was the real point.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、なんて言ったんだ？」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese:
「ね、春希…
あたしはまだ、ミイラ取りのままでいられてると思う？」
lines.english: “Tell me, Haruki… do you think I’m still the hunter, and not the one who’s been caught?”

lines.japanese: 「肝心なところぼかしたまま話を進めるな」
lines.english: “Don’t skip the important part and carry on as if I heard it.”

lines.japanese: 和泉の仕草、息遣い、口数、顔色、その他諸々…
lines.english: Izumi’s gestures, breathing, speech, complexion, and everything else…

lines.japanese:
そのどれを見ても、
さっきと全然違ってないように見えるのは、
俺の観察眼の限界なのか、それとも…
lines.english: If none of it looked the slightest bit different from before, was that merely the limit of my perception—or…?

lines.japanese: 「ま、別にそれはいいけどさ…何で駄目？」
lines.english: “Well, never mind. Why won’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでって…俺たちつきあってないだろ」
lines.english: “Because… we’re not dating.”

lines.japanese: そして俺の仕草、息遣い、口数、顔色、その他諸々…
lines.english: And my own gestures, breathing, speech, complexion, and everything else…

lines.japanese:
「別につきあわなくてもいいんだけど。
ただあたしは、ちょっと春希に深く関わりたいだけで」
lines.english: “We don’t have to date. I only want to get a little more deeply involved with you.”

lines.japanese:
「…意味わからん。
それって告白とどう違うんだよ？」
lines.english: “That makes no sense. How is that any different from telling me you have feelings for me?”

lines.japanese:
自分でも、まったく平常を保ってないと、
自信を持って言える今の精神状態は、
果たして和泉には、どう映ってるんだろうか…
lines.english: I could state with complete confidence that I was nowhere near composed. I wondered what Izumi saw when she looked at me.

lines.japanese:
「微妙に違うんだけど…
ま、どうしても定義がいるんなら、
別にそう取ってもらってもいいよ？」
lines.english: “There’s a subtle difference. But if you absolutely need a label, you can take it that way.”

lines.japanese: 「お前、なぁ…」
lines.english: “Honestly, you…”

lines.japanese:
勝負は、まだ続いてる。
ひたすら俺に不利な状況のままで。
lines.english: The contest continued, with the odds as crushingly against me as ever.

lines.japanese:
「別に、軽く考えればいいと思うよ？
それこそピザ代ってことにするとかさぁ」
lines.english: “You could keep it casual. Call it payment for the pizza, if you like.”

lines.japanese: 「俺がそういう割り切りできないって知らないか？」
lines.english: “You know I can’t separate things that neatly.”

lines.japanese:
「知ってるよ。
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はあるからね」
lines.english: “I know. I’m confident we’ve been involved enough for me to understand that much.”

lines.japanese: 千晶の脚が、ゆっくりと俺の膝をさすってくる。
lines.english: Chiaki’s leg slowly stroked my knee.

lines.japanese:
テーブルの上の表情は完全にいつも通りなのに、
テーブルの下ではまるで激情を隠そうとしない。
lines.english: Above the table, her face was perfectly ordinary. Beneath it, she made no attempt to conceal the force of her desire.

lines.japanese:
「だったら…そろそろ退いてくれ。
俺、お前のこと嫌いじゃないから
こういう会話続けるの辛いんだよ」
lines.english: “Then please back off. I don’t dislike you, and that’s exactly why continuing this conversation hurts.”

lines.japanese:
その和泉の二面的な行為についていけない俺は、
とっくに駆け引きの勝負では負けている。
lines.english: Unable to keep up with the two different Izumis above and below the table, I had already lost our game of wits.

lines.japanese:
観察眼もポーカーフェイスも、
使うことすら放棄してしまっている。
lines.english: I had abandoned even the attempt to observe her or maintain a poker face.

lines.japanese:
「なら、今からする質問に
真面目に答えたら許してあげる」
lines.english: “Then answer one question honestly, and I’ll let you go.”

lines.japanese: 「それって…」
lines.english: “You mean…?”

lines.japanese: 「ね、春希…あんた今、好きなコいる？」
lines.english: “Haruki… is there a girl you’re in love with now?”
“…Yes.”

lines.japanese: それでも…
lines.english: Even so…

lines.japanese:
勝負を放棄してでも、
守らなければならない気持ちがあったから。
lines.english: There was one feeling I had to protect, even if it meant forfeiting the game.

lines.japanese:
だからこそ、
その質問にだけは、逡巡は許されなかった。
和泉に対しても、そして…
lines.english: So on that question alone, I could not allow myself to hesitate. For Izumi’s sake, and for…

lines.japanese: 「…だったら何で引きこもってたの？」
lines.english: “Then why were you hiding in here?”

lines.japanese: 「振られた、から」
lines.english: “Because she rejected me.”

lines.japanese: 「…一進二退、かぁ」
lines.english: “One step forward and two back, huh?”

lines.japanese:
「なんだよその間違った日本語は？
しかも意味はそこはかとなく合ってるし…」
lines.english: “That’s not how the saying goes. Though annoyingly enough, it fits.”

lines.japanese: 「でもさ、それって余計あたしの出番じゃない？」
lines.english: “Doesn’t that make this even more my cue?”

lines.japanese: 「いや…違うよ」
lines.english: “No… it doesn’t.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まぁ、その…なんて言うか」
lines.english: “Well, because… how do I put this?”

lines.japanese:
「それでも、好きだから？
諦められないから？」
lines.english: “You still love her? You can’t give up?”
“…Yes.”

lines.japanese:
そんな強い決意を抱いてたくせに、
最後、全然締まらなかった。
lines.english: After all that grim determination, I made a complete mess of the finish.

lines.japanese:
自分で言えなかった。
最低だった。
lines.english: I couldn’t even say it myself. Pathetic.
“…I see.”

lines.japanese: 「すまん」
lines.english: “I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese:
「そこ謝るところじゃないから。
別にあたしショック受けてないし」
lines.english: “That isn’t something you apologize for. I’m not hurt or anything.”

lines.japanese: 「うん…」
lines.english: “Right…”

lines.japanese: けれど、ちゃんと相手には伝わったから。
lines.english: But at least she had understood.

lines.japanese:
それに、伝えたのが本人じゃなかったから、
今はそれでよしとさせて欲しい。
lines.english: And since she wasn’t the person I truly needed to say it to, I wanted to let that be enough for now.

lines.japanese: 「ん～、潮時かなぁ」
lines.english: “Mm… I guess this is where I stop.”

lines.japanese: いつの間にか、和泉の脚が俺から離れていた。
lines.english: At some point, Izumi’s leg had withdrawn from mine.

lines.japanese:
「モチーフとしては
ますます魅力的になっちゃったんだけど、
さすがにもう、追いかけられないよね」
lines.english: “You’ve become even more compelling as a subject, but I can hardly keep chasing you now.”

lines.japanese:
だらけたように全身の力を抜き、
天井を仰いで、何もかも終わったかのような
すがすがしい表情を見せる。
lines.english: She let every muscle go slack, tilted her head toward the ceiling, and wore a clear, refreshed expression, as though everything were over.

lines.japanese:
それは、今までのポーカーフェイスとは違ってたけど、
だからといってその心情が易々とくみ取れるほど、
和泉の内部構造は簡単じゃなかった。
lines.english: It was different from her poker face. That didn’t make the machinery inside Izumi simple enough for me to read.

lines.japanese:
「これであたしの大いなる野望は終わり…
ありがと春希、今まで夢見させてくれて」
lines.english: “And so ends my grand ambition. Thank you for letting me dream, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「本当にお前の言ってることは訳わからんな」
lines.english: “I never understand a word you say.”

lines.japanese:
「世の中には知らない方が幸せなこともあるよ？
例えばあたしがとんでもない悪女だとか」
lines.english: “Ignorance can be bliss, you know. For instance, maybe I’m a truly terrible woman.”

lines.japanese:
「あるわけないだろそんなこと…
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はある」
lines.english: “As if you could be. I’m confident we’ve been involved enough for me to know that much.”

lines.japanese: 「………ごめんね」
lines.english: “…I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese:
和泉がその言葉を漏らした後、
俺たちの間を苦い、けれど優しい沈黙が支配する。
lines.english: After Izumi let those words escape, a silence settled between us—bitter, but gentle.

lines.japanese:
さっきまでの激闘を覚えているものは、もういない。
…テーブルの上にまき散らされたカード以外には。
lines.english: Nothing remained to testify to the battle we had just fought except the cards scattered across the table.

lines.japanese:
「本当に泊まっていかなくていいのか？
もう終電ないだろ？」
lines.english: “Are you sure you don’t want to stay? The last train’s gone.”

lines.japanese: 「だからわざと聞こえないように呟くのはよせ」
lines.english: “Stop muttering under your breath so I can’t hear.”

lines.japanese: 食事も済んで、酒も入って、ゲームに興じて。
lines.english: We had eaten, drunk, and played games.

lines.japanese:
もう後は寝るだけってところで、
和泉はいきなり帰り支度を始めた。
lines.english: Just when there was nothing left to do but sleep, Izumi abruptly began preparing to leave.

lines.japanese:
「さすがに別の女に操立ててる男の部屋に
泊まるのは辛いよ…」
lines.english: “Staying in the apartment of a man who’s staying faithful to another woman would be a little painful.”

lines.japanese:
…まぁ、経緯を考えれば
ちっともいきなりじゃないと言えばそうなんだけど。
lines.english: Though after everything that had happened, perhaps it wasn’t abrupt at all.

lines.japanese: 「お前らしくないな、和泉」
lines.english: “That doesn’t sound like you, Izumi.”

lines.japanese: 「寝ぼけていつの間にか入っちゃってても悪いし」
lines.english: “I might crawl into your bed in my sleep. That would be awkward.”

lines.japanese: 「…お前らしいな、和泉」
lines.english: “Now that sounds like you.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ…またな」
lines.english: “Y-yeah. See you.”

lines.japanese: いつもの軽口も、これ以上盛り上がることはなく。
lines.english: Our usual banter went no further.

lines.japanese:
淡々と、ちょっとだけ情緒的に、
俺たちは、軽く手を振りあう。
lines.english: Matter-of-factly, with just a trace of feeling, we exchanged small waves.
“Haruki…?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese:
そんな軽い別れに、
少しは寂しさを感じてくれたのか…
lines.english: Perhaps even she felt a little lonely at so casual a farewell.

lines.japanese:
「あたしはね、
本当はあんたの想いの深さを知ってるよ？」
lines.english: “The truth is, I know how deep your feelings run.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「物語にしても遜色のない、
あんたたちの綺麗な想いを知ってるよ？」
lines.english: “I know how beautiful your feelings for each other are—beautiful enough for any story.”

lines.japanese: 「何…言ってんだ？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
和泉は、少し熱めに、
さらに情緒的に目を潤ませる。
lines.english: Izumi’s eyes grew damp, her gaze a little more heated now, a little more openly emotional.

lines.japanese:
「ここまで引っ張ったんだ…
どうせなら、最後まで突っ走って
綺麗な物語を綺麗なまま完結させて欲しいな」
lines.english: “You’ve carried it this far. You might as well run all the way to the end and let the beautiful story end beautifully.”

lines.japanese: 「和泉…お前」
lines.english: “Izumi… you…”

lines.japanese: 「そしたら今度こそ…」
lines.english: “Then, next time, I’ll finally…”

lines.japanese:
けれど、最後の最後まで、
大事なところは声に出さず、
最後の一線を越えないまま。
lines.english: But even at the very end, she left the essential words unspoken and refused to cross that final line.

lines.japanese:
和泉は、自分の手の内を明かさないまま、
その想いを昇華させてしまった。
lines.english: Without ever showing her hand, Izumi found a way to sublimate those feelings.

lines.japanese:
「おやすみ、あたしの神様。
あなたを見つめ続けてきたこの数年間、
本当に楽しかったよ」
lines.english: “Good night, my god. These past few years I’ve spent watching you have truly been wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 数日間の間違いだろ…それ。
lines.english: You mean the past few days.
